annotation.title_clean: Durkheim's Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.title_en: Durkheim's Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Unknown (chapter in Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, vol. 366)
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 366: Social Robots in Social Institutions (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Conference chapter applying Durkheim's theory of the division of labor to robotics innovation. It uses his three social pathologies (forced division of labor, excessive division of labor, anomie) as a framework for assessing the social and ethical impacts of workplace robots and for socially responsible innovation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Durkheim's theory offers an interpretive framework for the social impacts of robots in the workplace.
Forced division of labor, excessive division of labor and anomie are pathologies robots may contribute to.
The shift from mechanical to organic solidarity can be disrupted by robot deployment.
Argues for socially responsible innovation that accounts for Durkheim's insights.
